title: One World Ocean
objective: After this level you can name the five oceans and explain why they are really one connected ocean.
summary: Seas are smaller corners of the ocean, usually partly enclosed by land, and the five named oceans are regions of one ocean. At its deepest, it could swallow Everest.

cards.headline: There is a sea with no shore anywhere.
cards.body: Picture a sea and you probably see a beach around the edge. The Sargasso Sea, out in the Atlantic, has no coastline at all. Ocean currents alone draw its edges. So what makes a sea a sea, and where does one ocean end?

cards.headline: Seas are corners of the ocean
cards.body: A sea is smaller than an ocean. It usually lies where land and ocean meet, and it's typically partly enclosed by land. If the ocean is a big house, seas are its alcoves. The Sargasso is the odd one out: the only sea with no land boundary at all. It's a room whose walls are made of moving water.

cards.headline: Five names, still one ocean
cards.body: Remember Level 1's oceans? From largest to smallest: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic. They're not five tanks. They're connected regions of one global ocean, divided by lines people drew. That's how a sea can float in the middle of the Atlantic with no shore. The borders were only ever on paper.

cards.fact: The ocean's deepest known point is about 11 km down.
cards.context: It's called Challenger Deep, in the Pacific's Mariana Trench. Level 7's Mount Everest stands about 8,849 m tall. Set it on the bottom of Challenger Deep and its peak would still be about 2 km underwater. Most of the ocean is shallower, with an average depth of about 3,700 m. That's still a long way to swim.

cards.headline: One ocean: explored
learned: Seas are smaller, usually partly enclosed by land
The Sargasso Sea has no shore at all
Five named oceans, one connected ocean
Challenger Deep is about 11 km down

questions.prompt: What makes the Sargasso Sea different from every other sea?

options.label: It is fresh water
options.rationale: It is part of the salty Atlantic.

options.label: It is the deepest sea
options.rationale: Depth is not what sets it apart.

questions.explanation: Every other sea is bounded at least partly by land; the Sargasso is defined only by ocean currents.

questions.prompt: A ship sails from the Atlantic into the Indian Ocean. What does it actually cross?

options.label: A line people drew on maps
An underwater wall between basins
options.rationale: No wall: the water is continuous.

options.label: A strip of fresh water
options.rationale: The oceans share the same salty water.

options.label: A change in sea level
options.rationale: The oceans are connected; there is no step.

questions.explanation: The named oceans are regions of one global ocean. The borders between them are lines people drew.

questions.prompt: From Level 7: if Mount Everest stood on the floor of Challenger Deep, where would its peak be?

options.label: About 2 km above the waves
options.rationale: Challenger Deep is deeper than Everest is tall.

options.label: Just poking out of the water
options.rationale: There is about 2 km of water to spare.

options.label: At the average depth of the ocean

questions.explanation: Challenger Deep is about 11 km deep and Everest about 8,849 m tall, so the peak would sit about 2 km below the surface.
